title: Gu Wanyue (女妖 骨婉约) - Location, Tactics & Rewards
description: Gu Wanyue (女妖 骨婉约) in Phantom Blade Zero - where the fight happens, what it drops, and how its attack patterns are countered, including the red and blue flash tells.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Gu Wanyue (女妖 骨婉约) is a story encounter in Pangzhen, found at The Singing Pond bell.

sections.title: Where to Find the Gu Wanyue (女妖 骨婉约)
sections.content:
Location: The Singing Pond bell.

Appears in: Pangzhen.

sections.title: Weaknesses and Counters
sections.content:
There is no weakness table for this fight because there is no damage-type system to fill one in: nothing here resists, absorbs or is immune to anything, and a chart that says otherwise has been inferred from how the boss looks. Read the fight by attack colour instead - red must be dodged, blue must be deflected, purple means it has just parried you and a counter is already coming. The full explanation is on the combat system.

It is mandatory, so it cannot be walked past - the fight is worth learning rather than trying to out-level.

sections.title: Rewards
sections.content: No drop is recorded for this encounter in the sources checked, so none is listed. That is a gap in the record rather than a statement that it drops nothing.

sections.title: How to Beat the Gu Wanyue (女妖 骨婉约)
sections.content:
Gu Wanyue is the fight that teaches the game's defensive loop, because for most of it she cannot be damaged at all: while the smoke effect is on her body, attacks pass through. The only way in is to empty her Sha-Chi bar, and the only way to empty it is to parry and dodge correctly.

The rhythm is drain, stagger, burst: parry the sleeve strings, deflect the projectile, dodge the grabs, then unload everything the moment she staggers. Back off the instant she recovers and start again. Healing before the arena, not during it, is the difference between a clean attempt and a wipe.

Attacks worth knowing

AttackWhat it doesAnswer
Sleeve swipesClose-to-mid range stringsParry - this is the main Sha-Chi drain
Blue projectileSlow fireballPerfect parry to deflect it back; applies vulnerability
Neck BreakerHandstand leap onto your shoulders, red flashDodge - removes a large chunk of her bar
Darkness phaseArena fades to blackHold block, react to the flash, do not parry blind

What works

  • She is immune to damage until her Sha-Chi bar breaks; parries and perfect dodges are the only way to drain it.
  • Deflect the blue-flash projectile back at her - it marks her and opens the biggest window.
  • Dodge every red-flash grab, especially the handstand neck-breaker; a clean dodge removes a large chunk of her bar.
  • When the arena goes dark she can attack from any angle: hold block and react to the flash rather than parrying blind.

sections.title: Status
sections.content: No. 26 of 60 in the progression order, in Pangzhen. Before it: Wu Xuan, the Fallen General (堕落将军 武轩). After it: Xie Qiudong, the Divine Healer (神医 谢秋冬). The roster by region is on the boss list, and the fights that can be lost by leaving a region early are on the order page. Location and drops come from the shipped game; patch 1.0302256 is the most recent change to any boss behaviour and it touched only Hua.
